proposals.title: A whole house for what one room cost
proposals.line: I moved to a cheaper city with my remote job, and my payment on a three-bedroom house is about what I paid for one room before.

examples.name: Tulsa Remote
examples.outcome: A $10,000 grant for remote workers who move to Tulsa for a year; more than 3,300 workers since 2019, about 90% stay longer than a year; one participant's mortgage on a three-bedroom home roughly equals what she paid for a single room in Los Angeles

proposals.title: Good city-owned apartments for people with ordinary incomes
proposals.line: My city builds and owns well-kept apartments where people like me pay rent we can afford, the way Vienna has for about a century.

examples.name: Vienna city-owned and co-operative flats
examples.outcome: About 220,000 city-owned flats and 200,000 co-operative flats; eligibility needs two years living in Vienna and income below a limit

examples.name: Housing Opportunities Commission mixed-income social housing
examples.outcome: The county housing agency set up a Housing Production Fund in 2021 to build mixed-income apartments it owns; the first, The Laureate, has 268 homes, with affordable and market-rate homes looking the same and higher rents offsetting lower ones

proposals.title: Knowing what my rent should be before I sign
proposals.line: Before I sign a lease, I can see what similar apartments nearby rent for and who owns the building, so I know whether the price is fair.

examples.name: JustFix tenant tools
examples.outcome: Free tools to order an apartment's rent history by mail or text, look up who owns a building and their other properties (Who Owns What), and send a repair letter by certified mail

examples.name: Conny and Germany's rent brake
examples.outcome: In tight markets, rent on a new lease may be no more than 10% above the local comparative rent from the city's rent index; Conny checks a tenant's rent, sends the formal complaint, and charges only if the rent is reduced

overlaps.title: Getting back rent I was overcharged
overlaps.reason: Both rest on knowing a home's legal or comparable rent, before and after signing.

proposals.title: Paying less rent in exchange for help around the house
proposals.line: I rent a spare room from an older homeowner and pay less because I help with groceries, chores, and yard work.

examples.name: Nesterly home-sharing matches
examples.outcome: Matches people who have spare rooms with renters for stays of a month or more; guests can agree to help around the home in exchange for lower rent; either side can end with 30 days' notice

examples.name: HomeShare Vermont
examples.outcome: Nonprofit matching housemates since 1982 across 12 of Vermont's 14 counties; people choose whom they live with after screening

overlaps.title: Splitting rent with a housemate I chose
overlaps.reason: Both are home-sharing, and trading help for lower rent is one form of sharing with a chosen housemate.

proposals.title: A lower rent at my next lease renewal
proposals.line: When my lease came up, I showed my landlord similar listings and my record of paying on time, and we settled on less than they first asked.

examples.name: Avail survey of renters negotiating rent
examples.outcome: Success rate for negotiating lower rent rose from 17% in October 2022 to just over 25% in April 2023; only 28% negotiated their most recent renewal

proposals.title: Enough new homes nearby that rents stop climbing
proposals.line: My city allowed more apartments and duplexes to be built, and rents near me rose much less than in the rest of the state.

examples.name: Minneapolis land-use reforms
examples.outcome: From 2017 to 2022 the city permitted about 21,000 new homes, about 12% more housing against about 4% statewide, and rent growth ran 13 percentage points below the state average; renters pay about $1,700 a year less than if rents had tracked the state

examples.name: Backyard homes (ADUs) in Los Angeles
examples.outcome: Over 25,000 accessory dwelling units (backyard homes) permitted in the city since 2017, after California made them easier to build

proposals.title: Getting back rent I was overcharged
proposals.line: I checked my apartment's legal rent and rent history, and my landlord had to lower my rent and pay back part of what I'd overpaid.

examples.name: Conny and Germany's rent brake
examples.outcome: In tight markets, rent on a new lease may be no more than 10% above the local comparative rent from the city's rent index; Conny checks a tenant's rent, sends the formal complaint, and charges only if the rent is reduced

examples.name: JustFix tenant tools

proposals.title: Owning an affordable home through a land trust
proposals.line: I bought a home through a community land trust at a price I could afford, and when I sell I keep part of the gain.

examples.name: Champlain Housing Trust shared-equity homes
examples.outcome: Study of 205 resales of homes developed 1988 to 2008: the average seller left nearly $14,000 richer after about 5.4 years, and 73% bought another home when they left

proposals.title: Paying about a third of my income on rent
proposals.line: My rent is set at about 30% of what I earn, so the rest of my paycheck goes to food, bills, and savings.

examples.name: Housing Choice Voucher program (Section 8)
examples.outcome: About 2,000 local public housing agencies run it with HUD funding; the family typically pays about 30% of adjusted monthly income, up to 40%, and the agency pays the landlord the rest

examples.name: Brooke Amendment, origin of the 30% rent rule
examples.outcome: Capped public housing rent at 25% of a tenant's income in 1969; raised to 30% in 1981, which became the common rule of thumb for affordable rent

overlaps.title: This month's rent paid while I catch up
overlaps.reason: Both are rent paid partly by an assistance program; one is short-term help, the other a lasting subsidy.

proposals.title: Yearly rent increases capped by law
proposals.line: My rent can only go up by a set amount each year, so I never open a renewal letter to a jump I can't pay.

examples.name: Oregon statewide rent stabilization
examples.outcome: Yearly rent increases are capped at 7% plus inflation, never more than 10%; the cap was 9.5% for 2026 and is 10% for 2027

examples.name: Stanford study of San Francisco's 1994 rent control expansion
examples.outcome: Covered tenants saved roughly $2,300 to $6,600 a year, but rent-controlled units fell about 25% from 1994 to 2010 and later renters paid about 5% more

overlaps.title: My building's tenants keeping our rent steady together
overlaps.reason: Both end with rent that holds steady; one gets there by law and one by tenants negotiating together.

proposals.title: This month's rent paid while I catch up
proposals.line: I found local rental assistance through 211, and this month's rent is covered while I get back on my feet.

examples.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rent help page
examples.outcome: Points renters to state, tribal, and local rental assistance, 211, HUD-approved housing counselors, year-round utility help through LIHEAP (the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program), and housing choice vouchers

overlaps.title: Paying about a third of my income on rent
overlaps.reason: Both are rent paid partly by an assistance program; one is short-term help, the other a lasting subsidy.

proposals.title: Saving money while I live with family for a while
proposals.line: I moved back in with my parents for now, and the money I'd have spent on rent is going into savings for a place of my own.

examples.name: Pew Research Center on multigenerational homes
examples.outcome: Among adults 25 and older living with a parent, 57% of those ages 25 to 39 say finances are a major reason, compared with 31% of older adults

proposals.title: Sharing a house with friends as we get older
proposals.line: A few friends and I share one house as we age, and splitting the costs means none of us is stretched thin.

examples.name: Older women sharing homes as housemates (AARP report)
examples.outcome: 57% of women 50 and older would consider living with a friend as they age (2024 AARP survey); about 1 in 4 adults 50 and older would consider renting part of their home to a nonfamily member (July 2026); Colorado's 2024 law removed local caps on unrelated people living together

overlaps.reason: Sharing a house with friends is a version of splitting rent with a chosen housemate.

proposals.title: My building's tenants keeping our rent steady together
proposals.line: My neighbors and I formed a tenants union, and now our rent holds steady and repairs get done by a set deadline.

examples.name: KC Tenants rent strike at Independence Towers
examples.outcome: After an eight-month rent strike, tenants won a contract that held rents steady, removed some extra fees, and set a deadline for repairs; KC Tenants, founded in 2019, has more than 10,000 members
